# Aster pump: code reference
This fictional manual covers the Aster station pump. Operators distinguish the live pressure reading from the test reading. Test readings never authorize a live restart. Keep the maintenance log with the device serial number and record the current shift before changing settings.

## Starting the Aster controller
The controller checks pressure before enabling the pump. The maintenance branch returns a diagnostic result without activating hardware. A missing reading is a hard failure. Callers must handle the exception and must not replace a missing reading with zero. This distinction matters during startup.

## Retry policy
The Aster pump startup caller waits 45 seconds after a blocked attempt. A diagnostic-only result is not a blocked attempt. Retries require a new reading; cached readings cannot be reused. The retry counter is reset only after a successful live start, never after a diagnostic run.

## Contact
For an unreadable Aster label, stop the pump and contact the station desk. This document contains fictional operational information for retrieval experiments only. It is not an engineering procedure for real equipment.

# Aster pump: table reference
This fictional manual covers the Aster station pump. Operators distinguish the live pressure reading from the test reading. Test readings never authorize a live restart. Keep the maintenance log with the device serial number and record the current shift before changing settings.

## Aster limits
Use the active-mode row for the live pump. The standby row applies only after shutdown. The inspection row is used during supervised maintenance and does not authorize production. Each row specifies its own maximum reading, wait duration, and required permit. Never combine cells from different rows.

| Mode | Maximum reading | Wait seconds | Permit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| active | 18 | 45 | amber |
| standby | 25 | 60 | white |
| inspection | 29 | 75 | black |

## Expired permits
An expired amber permit invalidates the active row for the Aster pump. Renew it at the station desk before retrying. Standby limits remain valid while renewal is pending. The desk cannot waive the active maximum; approval restores permission but never changes the table values.

## Contact

# Aster pump: cross reference reference
This fictional manual covers the Aster station pump. Operators distinguish the live pressure reading from the test reading. Test readings never authorize a live restart. Keep the maintenance log with the device serial number and record the current shift before changing settings.

## Release procedure R-Aster
Release of the Aster pump requires the amber permit defined in section P-Aster. The release operator must also complete the waiting rule in section W-Aster. A signature on the shift log records completion; it does not replace either prerequisite. Training releases follow a separate procedure and cannot authorize a live device.

## Archive retention
Archive completed shift logs for fourteen days in the local cabinet. Copy only the serial number into the central index. The archive clerk checks page counts at the end of each shift. Missing pages require an incident note, but the archive process cannot issue permits or change device waiting rules.

## P-Aster: Permit definition
The amber permit requires two signatures: the operator and the duty engineer. This permit applies to the Aster pump only. A training supervisor cannot substitute for the duty engineer. Both signatures must be dated during the current shift. An older signed permit expires at shift handover.

## W-Aster: Waiting rule
Wait 45 seconds after the pressure falls below 18 before release. Restart the timer whenever the reading rises above the limit. The operator records the final uninterrupted interval in the shift log. The timer is a prerequisite separate from the permit signatures.

## Contact
For an unreadable Aster label, stop the pump and contact the station desk. This document contains fictional operational information for retrieval experiments only. It is not an engineering procedure for real equipment.
